plain.text: Some Pharisees tested Jesus by asking if a man may divorce his wife. Jesus asked what Moses commanded. They said Moses allowed a certificate of divorce. Jesus said Moses wrote this because of their hard hearts. From the beginning, God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh. "What God has joined together, let no one separate." In private he told the disciples that divorcing and remarrying is adultery.

People brought little children for Jesus to bless, but the disciples scolded them. Jesus was indignant. "Let the little children come to me. Don't stop them, for God's kingdom belongs to such as these." Anyone who will not receive the kingdom like a little child will never enter it. He took the children in his arms and blessed them.

A man ran up and knelt before Jesus: "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?" Jesus listed some commandments. The man said he had kept them since he was young. Jesus looked at him and loved him. "One thing you lack," he said. "Go, sell everything, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me." The man went away sad, because he was very rich. Jesus said it is hard for the rich to enter God's kingdom, harder than for a camel to go through the eye of a needle. The astonished disciples asked who could be saved. Jesus said, "With people it is impossible, but not with God. All things are possible with God." He promised that those who leave things behind for him will receive far more, now and in the age to come. "Many who are first will be last, and the last first."
On the road up to Jerusalem, Jesus told the twelve a third time what would happen: he would be handed over, condemned, mocked, flogged and killed, and after three days he would rise.

James and John asked to sit at Jesus' right and left in his glory. Jesus asked if they could share his suffering. The other disciples were angry with them. Jesus called them together and said, "Among the nations, rulers lord it over people. It must not be like that among you. Whoever wants to be great must be your servant. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."

Leaving Jericho, Jesus passed a blind beggar named Bartimaeus. He shouted, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" People told him to be quiet, but he shouted louder. Jesus stopped and called him. Bartimaeus threw off his cloak and came. "What do you want me to do for you?" Jesus asked. "Teacher, I want to see." "Go," said Jesus, "your faith has healed you." Immediately he could see, and he followed Jesus along the road.

summary.bigIdea: God's kingdom belongs to those who receive it like children, and Jesus came to serve and give his life.
points: Jesus welcomes children and says the kingdom belongs to such as these.
A rich man walks away sad, but "all things are possible with God."
Jesus came "not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
summary.reflection: Jesus asked Bartimaeus, "What do you want me to do for you?" How would you answer?
